2025.05.09 19:03:44 +0530 Order Sheet 09/05/2025 Heard Mr. Mayank Chandrakar, learned counsel for the petitioner.

Also heard Mr. Shailendra Sharma,
learned Panel Lawyer, appearing for respondents No. 1 & 2/State.

It is argued by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the respondent No. 3 has made a written complaint before the concerning Police Station by stating that the Khomesh Pandey@ Golu vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93861578/
1 petitioner has shown the piece of land to the complainant on the pretext that he is owner of the land bearing Khasra No. 325 situated at village Baghera.

entities.text: Khomesh Pandey@ Golu vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, on enquiry from the concerned authorities it was found that said land does not belongs to the petitioner and he has shown forged rin pustika to the complainant.
On the basis of aforesaid allegation, FIR has been registered against the petitioner for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468 & 471 of the IPC.
He further argued that the said amount was borrowed by the petitioner instead of receiving advance amount on pretext of selling the subject land.

The petitioner had already returned the borrowed amount and to that effect the complainant has submitted an affidavit before the learned trial Court by stating no objection if bail will be granted to the petitioner.

That on the basis of the same this Hon'ble Court was pleased enough to allow bail application i.e. MCRC No. 8685 of 2024 filed by the petitioner, but out of greed now the complainant is not ready and willing to appear before the learned trial Court for filing an application for compounding of criminal cases and in absence of the complainant the learned trial Court is not accepting the application for compounding of criminal cases.

It is further submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that looking to the entire facts and circumstances of the case the entire allegation is baseless and even if the entire prosecution case will be taken as it is, then it is hardly a case of civil nature,
therefore, continuation of criminal case against the petitioner is nothing, but an abuse of process of law.
Issue notice to the respondents by ordinary as well as registered posts.

Learned State counsel appears and accepts notice on behalf of respondents No. 1 & 2,
therefore, issuance of notice to them, is dispensed with.
Process fee be paid within a week only for respondent No. 2.
Notice be made returnable in four weeks.

Two weeks' time is granted to the learned State counsel as well as respondent No. 2 to file their reply- affidavit and thereafter,
two weeks' time is granted to the learned counsel for the petitioner to file rejoinder-affidavit.
List this matter thereafter.
Till the next date of listing, the proceedings pending before the learned trial Court in Criminal Case No. RCC/23870/2024 against the petitioner, shall remain stayed.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (Arvind Kumar Verma) (Ramesh Sinha)
